hero: In a small laboratory room of a public hospital in Marikina after a flood, a Filipino nephrology fellow and a young Filipino intern look through a light microscope at a urine slide, beside a benchtop centrifuge and a clear cup of dark tea-colored urine; rain-washed windows, overcast light, concentrated mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Each urine cast and cell type points to a compartment of kidney injury.
figures.content: Grid of 8 circular microscope-field panels, each with a label underneath. 1 'Hyaline cast - concentrated urine, often normal'. 2 'Muddy brown granular cast - acute tubular necrosis'. 3 'Renal tubular epithelial cell - tubular injury'. 4 'Red cell cast - glomerulonephritis'. 5 'Acanthocyte (ring with blebs) - glomerular bleeding; >=5% of RBCs: sensitivity 52%, specificity 98%'. 6 'White cell cast - interstitial nephritis or pyelonephritis'. 7 'Fatty cast / oval fat body (Maltese cross under polarized light) - nephrotic syndrome'. 8 'Pigmented granular cast - rhabdomyolysis or hemolysis'. Footer: 'Spin 10 mL fresh urine; scan coverslip edges on low power.'

figures.teaches: Kidney size, cortical echogenicity and the collecting system distinguish chronic, acute and obstructive patterns.
figures.content: Five side-by-side sagittal kidney sketches in grayscale ultrasound style. 1 'Normal: normal size, cortex less bright than liver'. 2 'Chronic: small, thin bright cortex - next: acute change on top?'. 3 'Acute or infiltrative: normal or large, swollen - next: sediment, protein'. 4 'Hydronephrosis: dilated pelvis and calyces - next: bladder? unilateral or bilateral? drain'. 5 'Asymmetric: one small kidney - next: renovascular, reflux scarring'. Caution strip: 'Early or dry obstruction may show little dilation.'

card: A nephrology fellow and intern at a microscope beside a cup of tea-colored urine, no text.
